## Example 4.6 · Summation notation {#ss4-example-4-6-a .ar-lesson .ar-summation-slide}

Evaluate the following expressions:

<div class="ar-summation-task"><span>a)</span><span data-math="\displaystyle\sum\limits_{k=1}^{40}(2k+3)">sum from k equals 1 to 40 of 2k plus 3</span></div>

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
$$5+7+9+\cdots+83$$

:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 23 · Example 4.6(a)</p>

::: notes

Preserve the source expression and index k. The first summand is 2(1)+3=5, the last is 2(40)+3=83, and there are 40 terms. Sum=40(5+83)/2=1760. The expansion is an optional scaffold after independent thinking, not an automatic answer.

:::
